recalled_knowledge.item: Colouring/marking theorem for superposed independent Poisson processes: P(component H | observed point) = mu_H p_H(D) / sum_H' mu_H' p_H'(D)
A Poisson count n with expectation a*k and a log-uniform (1/k) prior yields a Gamma(n, scale 1/a) posterior on k; for n = 2, a = 3.23 the mean is 0.62 and the 95% point 1.47
Kullback-Leibler divergence KL(p||q) = sum p ln(p/q) as the information gained when the posterior moves from q to p
